hints: Picture one typical chromosome in a white blood cell and count how many of each part it has: how many centromeres, how many telomeres (look at the ends), how many chromatids, and how many DNA molecules?

Remember that histones are the tiny packaging proteins that DNA wraps around all along its length, so ask yourself whether there will be just a few or millions of them compared to one centromere per chromosome.
walkthrough:
**Start with the whole cell**

A human white blood cell is a normal diploid somatic cell, so it has 46 chromosomes. Think of each chromosome as the unit to count from. This gives us our baseline numbers.

**Count parts per chromosome**

For one unreplicated chromosome: there is 1 centromere, 1 chromatid containing 1 DNA molecule, 2 telomeres (one at each end), and huge numbers of histone proteins packaging that long DNA. So per cell: centromere = 46, DNA molecule = 46, chromatid = 46, telomere = $46 \times 2 = 92$, histone protein = millions.

**Put in least to most order**

Least numerous are centromere and DNA molecule (about 46), then telomere (about 92), then chromatid (46 if unreplicated, 92 if replicated for division), and by far the most numerous is histone protein. Only option A goes small to huge in the correct direction: centromere to chromatid to histone protein.

options.A: Correct. Centromeres are fewest (one per chromosome), chromatids are equal or double that, and histone proteins are millions, so this is least to most.
options.B: Incorrect. A chromosome has 1 DNA molecule but 2 telomeres, so telomere is more numerous than DNA molecule, but centromere (1 per chromosome) is not more numerous than telomere.
options.C: Incorrect. Histone proteins are the most numerous of all by far, so they cannot be first (least numerous) in the list.
options.D: Incorrect. Telomeres (2 per chromosome) are more numerous than centromeres (1 per chromosome), so starting with telomere as least is backwards.
